question: A furniture store marks its items at 80% above the cost price. They offer a discount of 30% on the marked price. If a customer receives an additional loyalty discount of ₹250, and the store still makes a 12% profit on the cost price, what is the cost price of the furniture item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) be 100%.

Marked Price (MP) = 180% (since markup is 80% above CP).

Selling Price (SP) after 30% discount = 180% × 0.7 = 126%.

With an additional profit of 12%, the actual SP = CP + 12% profit = 112%.

The difference in SP represents the loyalty discount: 126% − 112% = 14%.

CP (100%) = (₹250 ÷ 14) × 100 ≈ ₹1,785.71.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,785.71.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP
 
 SP
 
 MP
 

 Markup: +80%
 

 Discount: -30% & -₹250
 

 Profit: +12%

**Given:**

Markup = 80%

Discounts = 30% and an additional loyalty discount = ₹250

Profit = 12%

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

SP = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100) − Loyalty Discount

SP = CP × (1 + Profit% ÷ 100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100x.

⇒ MP = 100x × 1.80 = 180x

⇒ SP after standard 30% discount = 180x × (1 − 0.30) = 180x × 0.70 = 126x

⇒ Final SP = 126x − 250

⇒ According to the profit margin, SP = 100x × 1.12 = 112x

⇒ Equating the selling prices: 126x − 250 = 112x

⇒ 126x − 112x = 250

⇒ 14x = 250

⇒ x = 250 ÷ 14 = 125 ÷ 7

⇒ CP = 100x = 100 × (125 ÷ 7) = 12500 ÷ 7

⇒ CP ≈ ₹1,785.71

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,785.71.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. Net Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (a × b)÷100]%.

Direct CP to MP Ratio

When Profit% (P) and Discount% (D) are given, their relationship is simply derived as CP ÷ MP = (100 − D) ÷ (100 + P).
